summary: One immutable live-HEAD content observation is the authority for every worktree reclaim, destroy, and audit gate: the checked-out branch or detached tip, its SHA, and the clean-tree fact, read once before any effect, while the claim keeps its branch and base identity. Directory-removal proof is separate from stored-ref deletion: a stored ref is deleted only under its own durability proof with its tip pinned by the exact refs/heads path, the default-ref ownership guard runs before every deletion candidate against defaults established independently of the caller, a divergent live branch and a symbolic stored ref are retained, and unestablished ownership — including an empty set no observation established — fails closed by retaining refs without blocking a proven-durable live removal. One durable bounded plan, decoded from the committed facts, drives the first native execution and every replay: the retry never repins the live HEAD, replays the recorded force and approval, refuses a surviving directory whose content changed, and deletes through one pinned no-deref argv update-ref. Current ownership is re-derived before deletion: the protected default set is re-established from the repository as it stands and an unestablishable set fails closed. Complete pre-deletion inventory and symbolic HEAD observations must report no holder among the listed worktrees. This observed absence does not atomically exclude concurrent checkouts; it applies only at the points when those HEADs were observed, not throughout deletion or to later checkouts. When the post-deletion observation finds a listed HEAD naming the deleted branch, it records restoration debt. A successful create-only update restores that checkout at the immutable pinned tip; failed observation or restoration leaves durable, audit-visible recovery debt, not proof of successful restoration. A concurrently rebuilt ref remains unchanged. A malformed or incomplete inventory establishes no holder absence at the observed points. An absent ref settles only when complete inventory observations report no listed holder at those points; a replay resolves recorded recovery debt instead of treating unobserved absence as completion. Every retention, deletion debt, and native protection holds one durable outcome row keyed by the claim generation, settled by an idempotent SQL-only fold behind the native run, so retentions, sticky identity protections, re-derived checkout and default protections, and owed deletions stay visible to the audit after directory removal and after a later claim, with SQL-only transactions and commit-before-native-removal preserved. Retained live refs carry no upper bound the claim surface owns, so a valid long live branch — including a reftable identity no loose pathname could hold — records its full identity without blocking removal. The durable owner of each ref's state is one recorded phase of seven — planned, checkout_proven_absent, deleted, restoration_owed, restored, retained_unproven, settled — moved only by the typed transition table: the ownership observation re-derives authorization from every pending phase and records the absent-ref verdict, the pinned deletion starts only from a persisted checkout_proven_absent, the post-deletion observation starts only from deleted, the create-only restoration starts only from restoration_owed, identity protection and completion are terminal, and a restored ref stays replayable because its checkout protection is re-derived. The settlement owner refuses moves the table does not admit; a settlement the row already holds converges with no new event and no mutation; any transition is authorized only by a fresh chronological settlement event whose identity derives from the durable predecessor and the per-ref event sequence, so a historical target-phase event never authorizes a reentry, event equivalence is never the authorization, and a log rebuild replays the same trajectory the live row followed, restoration debt included; and no settlement commits an unclosed fold guard.
title: Reclaim gates the live head and records retained refs
